cards.back: A pure, fully-tested core with no OS/framework dependencies, plugged into the world by thin 'adapter' layers (mic, hotkey, clipboard, camera). The core is testable without the hardware attached. Sidekit's mac/ is built this way.

cards.front: Why is .atlas/data/environment.json committed, but git.json is not?
cards.back: environment.json carries the *view* of your machine-local AI config (global ~/.claude memories, skills, MCP) into the cloud container, which can never read ~/.claude itself. git.json is volatile — regenerated on every sync — so it is gitignored.

cards.front: SM-2: how does the interval grow on correct answers?
cards.back: reps 0 → 1 day, reps 1 → 6 days, then interval × ease each time (ease ≈ 2.5, nudged up/down per grade, floored at 1.3). A lapse (Again) resets reps to 0 and shrinks ease by 0.2.

Each source is a small { id, layer, detect(), read() } object in an ordered array; the driver runs every adapter whose detect() is true and writes the union. Supporting a new source — or a whole different repo — means adding an adapter, not rewriting the driver.

When sync runs where ~/.claude isn't visible (cloud / fresh clone), it must NOT drop the machine-local items it captured earlier. It reads the prior committed environment.json, carries those items forward verbatim, relabels them 'local-only · last seen <date>', and never deletes them.
